html:
Jacques Cartier was a sailor from Saint-Malo in France who made three voyages to North America from 1534 to 1542 for Francis I. In 1534 he raised a cross at Gaspe and claimed the land for France.

In 1535 he sailed up the St Lawrence River to the Iroquoian villages of Stadacona, where Quebec City now stands, and Hochelaga, now Montreal. His guides used the word kanata, meaning village, and Cartier applied the name Canada to the whole region.

He kidnapped the chief Donnacona and others, who died in France. His attempt to found a colony in 1541 failed amid scurvy, cold and conflict, and the "diamonds" he brought home proved worthless. Lasting settlement waited for Champlain in 1608 and New France.
